message.subject: pplx-decider-v1.1-27b installed: :11449 BF16 native autojev, 46/46 hashes verified, smoke OK, stopped (start only with GPU otherwise free)
message.body:
pplx-decider-v1.1-27b is INSTALLED on marvin (192.168.0.90) as service pplx-decider-27b on :11449. BF16 reference precision, native autojev runtime, smoke-tested, now STOPPED. (Re: msg 01a128e3.)

## Lifecycle (start only when no other large GPU tenant is loaded; it needs ~52 GB of the 64 GB VRAM)
  ssh 192.168.0.90 'cd /var/opt/docker/ai/decision-models-next && sudo docker compose up -d pplx-decider-27b'   # ready in ~24 s
  ssh 192.168.0.90 'cd /var/opt/docker/ai/decision-models-next && sudo docker compose stop pplx-decider-27b'    # VRAM back to baseline (verified)
Ready means GET /health returns status "ready" (native) or GET /healthz returns status "ok". Requests are serialized:
the native server returns 529 "busy" if a request arrives while another is running, so send one at a time.

## API: the release's own autojev.server routes, unchanged (http://192.168.0.90:11449)
- POST /v1/systemone {"model": "pplx-decider-v1.1-27b" | "autojev-qwen3.8-27b" | "jev-latest", "state":..., "questions":{...}}.
  The response is the native {"model","answers","usage":{input_tokens, output_tokens:0}}. choice answers have
  probabilities by your criteria IDs, choice and confidence; noul answers have noul; score answers have probabilities,
  legend, score and confidence. The native request schema forbids extra fields: choice criteria 1-255 options,
  score criteria 2-10 levels, noul criteria {true,false} or omitted.
- Overflow: inputs over 8192 tokens are REJECTED with the native HTTP 422 "Question branch exceeds the 8192-token limit;
  no input was truncated." The native status is 422, not 400; I kept native semantics. An unknown model also returns 422.
- Added endpoints (read-only, outside the native app's behavior):
  - GET /healthz: revision, precision, attention_mode, pooling, temperature, limits, dtypes, device, torch/hip, load_s.
  - POST /v1/encoding: per-question input_tokens via DecisionModel.prepare, or the native rejection. No forward pass.
- The native GET /health and GET /v1/models are unchanged. The added model alias is "pplx-decider-v1.1-27b".

## Provenance and hashes
- Repo perplexity-ai/pplx-decider-v1.1-27b @ 6195aa55a72ae21e503c8a60198f7b390d42adb5 (ungated). All 46 files listed in
  release-manifest.json were verified against the manifest's sha256 and byte counts, twice: (a) against the Hub's LFS
  metadata before downloading, and (b) by re-hashing every downloaded file inside the volume (46/46 OK).
  This covers model-00001..00011 (e.g. 00001 871e1db3…462ef6, 00011 cdd6261a…94f), readout.safetensors 774eaded…16e49,
  tokenizer.json 6f32ce20…57706, decision_config.json 68d4a4c7…25e8 and the source/ files.
- The code is the release's own source/src/autojev, imported from the pinned snapshot via PYTHONPATH and not
  pip-installed, so it cannot drift from the weights.
- decision_config: step 2446, attention_mode noncausal_full_attention, pooling last, temperature 1.0087417621345625,
  255 single-token codes. The temperature is applied exactly once, in the native autojev.server.predict.
- Architecture: Qwen3_5Model, model_type qwen3_5, transformers 5.17.0 config: 64 text layers in a DeltaNet linear-attention
  and full-attention 3:1 pattern, hidden 5120, plus a vision tower. The release names the base "Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B"
  (revision 1d4bf0f2…); the config itself is a standard qwen3_5 checkpoint.

## Image and exact dependencies
- decision-models-pplx:local, image ID sha256:1ca2a7509863a7d1de08ad5ab5e002ca28cc0f878f648f4d971712dcb8916910.
  Built FROM the yomik ROCm base. The build aborts if torch is not ROCm or transformers is not 5.17.0.
- Release-pinned versions honored: transformers 5.17.0, accelerate 1.15.0, safetensors 0.8.0.
- Base versions kept (constraints): torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.1 (HIP 7.2.53211), torchvision 0.24.0+rocm7.2.1, numpy 2.4.4,
  pillow 12.1.1. Also tokenizers 0.23.2, huggingface_hub 1.30.0, fastapi 0.143.0, uvicorn 0.54.0, httpx 0.28.1,
  pydantic 2.14.0. Full freeze: /opt/resolved-deps-full.txt in the image.
- Files on marvin: /var/opt/docker/ai/decision-models-next/pplx/{Dockerfile,run_pplx.py}; the compose service is
  pplx-decider-27b; weights are in volume decision_models_pplx, mounted read-only. Container cap: mem_limit 24g with
  memswap_limit equal to it.

## Code review (pinned source, before execution)
- model.py and server.py: weights load through safetensors only (no pickle/torch.load). There is no network access when
  loading from a local checkpoint (AutoProcessor and the model are loaded from the snapshot; HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1). No
  subprocess or exec, and no trust_remote_code. The optional AUTOJEV_API_KEY bearer check is unset, so the API is
  LAN-open like the other classifiers.
- The training, data and report modules are not imported by the server path.

## Compatibility deviations (all disclosed; none change the decision semantics)
1. Weight loading. The native call Qwen3_5Model.from_pretrained(ckpt, dtype=bf16, attn_implementation="sdpa") followed by
   .to("cuda") was OOM-killed: transformers 5.17 keeps all 11 shards mmapped while copying, and host usage reached the
   24 GiB container cap 12 s in. The host was unaffected. The launcher replaces that one call with a strict GPU loader:
   it builds the same class from the same config on cuda:0 with weight init skipped, copies each tensor from
   safetensors.safe_open(device="cuda:0") one shard at a time, and asserts every key is loaded exactly once with an
   identical shape and dtype. Verified beforehand: 1183 checkpoint tensors map 1:1 to the model's state_dict, all BF16,
   with no fp32-kept modules and no transformers weight conversion for qwen3_5. The resulting weights therefore equal
   from_pretrained(dtype=bfloat16). Everything else (the readout load, the noncausal attention hook, pooling, the
   temperature) runs the native code unchanged.
2. Torch: ROCm 2.9.1 instead of the release's CUDA 2.14.0.
3. Kernels: flash-linear-attention and causal_conv1d are not installed (untested Triton kernels on gfx1151), so
   transformers uses its reference PyTorch chunk_gated_delta_rule and conv paths. This is mathematically the same
   operation but slower, and float rounding can differ slightly from the fla kernels.
4. Precision: BF16 throughout, the reference precision. No quantization and no offload.

## Smoke results (same ticket fixture as the other classifiers; cold = first request after load)
- Load 23.5 s. VRAM went from 4,111 MB to 56,524 MB after load (48.6 GB allocated by torch), peaking at 56,691 MB.
  The container peaked at 10.4 GiB host memory, mostly page cache, and host MemAvailable never fell below 41.5 GB.
- Cold 4.43 s / warm 1.41 s. department=billing (p=0.99992), wants_refund noul=0.99970; usage input_tokens 250.
- /v1/encoding on a 2-option question: 87 tokens OK. An oversized state (~13k words): ok:false, and /v1/systemone
  returned 422 with "no input was truncated". An unknown model name returned 422.
- After stop: VRAM back to 4,111 MB. restart policy "no". No scored benchmark was run.

## Limits
8192 tokens per question branch (text and images combined), 1-255 choice options, 2-10 score levels, up to 4 images
per request as base64 data URLs (natively capped at 2048x2048; the evaluated setup used 512x512, so use
max_image_pixels=512*512-sized images to match it).

Inventory: homelab-docs decision-models-inventory.md (classifiers group). The service stays stopped; cleanup is the owner's call.
